extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journal editors, research-integrity sleuths, and informed readers of biomedical research
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating a published clinical trial (biomedical journal article) for signs of data inconsistencies, reporting failures, image/data manipulation, trial-registration mismatches, conflicts of interest, and adherence to journal data-sharing policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age eligibility consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Study claimed to have enrolled only patients under 65 years old, but the accompanying data showed 127 patients older than 65 — described as a "complete mismatch."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that baseline demographic data (age distributions, inclusion/exclusion criteria) in shared datasets match the study's eligibility claims and the manuscript text. Discrepancies between claimed eligibility criteria and actual participant ages are strong signals of reporting error or data problems; such mismatches may alone justify retraction according to some commentators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sharing timing and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors reportedly did not share the data until after peer review; data were uploaded as a private file for editors only and only after final peer review were they uploaded in accordance with The BMJ's policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether authors complied with the journal's data-sharing policy and whether data were available to reviewers during peer review. Anti-patterns include uploading data only after acceptance or making data inaccessible to reviewers (private files). Timely, reviewer-accessible data reduces the risk that serious reporting issues go unnoticed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeated-record patterns / templated cut-and-paste
rubrics_metrics.description: A "curious repeating pattern of records" was found: every 101 records almost all values were identical, suggesting repeating or copied rows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scan datasets for periodic repetition, blockwise duplication, or identical sequences across records (e.g., every Nth row identical). Such patterns can indicate fabrication, copy-paste errors, or automated templating. Investigators should flag and request provenance/raw files when repetition is detected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improbable measurement distributions and rounding
rubrics_metrics.description: Almost all patients' weights — 288 of 334 reported cases — were integers, with multiples of five kilograms heavily over-represented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine numeric distributions for unnatural rounding, excessive integer values, or over-representation of round numbers (multiples of 5 or 10). These anomalies may indicate data fabrication, poor measurement practices, or data entry errors. Use simple descriptive stats and histograms to detect such issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial registration and enrollment consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Discrepancy between the number of subjects enrolled (420) and those disclosed during the trial registration (360).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare reported sample sizes, enrollment dates, and participant counts in the manuscript with trial registry entries. Unexplained differences in enrollment numbers or endpoints between registry and publication suggest selective reporting, protocol deviations, or misreporting that warrant clarification or correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Undisclosed conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential undisclosed conflict: an author (Anthony Mathur) is a shareholder and trustee of the Heart Cells Foundation, which funds a unit administering stem cell therapies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check author affiliations and financial interests for relationships (shareholder, trustee, consultant) that could influence study conduct or interpretation. Undisclosed COIs undermine credibility; journals and readers expect transparent disclosure and may treat undisclosed ties as a serious integrity concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior history of flagged concerns for authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Several authors (e.g., Armin Attar, Negar Azarpira) have multiple prior papers flagged on PubPeer for image duplication and data concerns (Attar: five other papers flagged; Azarpira: 36 papers flagged).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider authors' publication histories and previous flags or retractions as contextual evidence. A pattern of prior concerns increases the seriousness of newly detected anomalies and may prompt broader investigation of the authors' body of work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image duplication and data-integrity flags
rubrics_metrics.description: Other papers by the authors have been flagged for image duplication and data issues on PubPeer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect figures and images for duplication, manipulation, or reuse across papers. Image forensics and close visual comparison with prior publications can reveal integrity problems. Journals should investigate credible image-duplication allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction threshold for serious discrepancies
rubrics_metrics.description: Commentators argued that the age discrepancies alone should constitute a retraction; others stated the article "needs to be retracted urgently."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether detected errors undermine the main findings or the reliability of the reported results. Significant uncorrected discrepancies in core data (eligibility, primary outcomes, sample size) may meet the threshold for retraction rather than correction, especially if they call into question the validity of conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial responsibility and review concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal's clinical editor noted "serious concerns regarding the reporting and data sharing" in the first decision; questions raised whether data were available to reviewers during review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals and editors should ensure that data required by policy are accessible to reviewers and that concerns raised during review are resolved prior to publication. Documented editorial concerns about reporting or data-sharing should trigger additional checks or requests for raw data before acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors' responsiveness and transparency about investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors stated they were conducting an internal audit and reviewing inconsistencies, expected to take two to three weeks; some authors did not respond to email requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether authors promptly acknowledge concerns, share audit outcomes, and correct the record. Delayed, incomplete, or non-responsive behavior reduces trust and may necessitate editorial notices, expressions of concern, corrections, or retraction if issues remain unresolved.
